definition_en: Scammers pose as insurers, banks, payment platforms or other financial institutions and use phishing texts, calls or fake websites to obtain personal data, passwords or money.
how_it_works_en: Scammers send texts claiming that a policy or account has a problem, and lure victims to a phishing link to enter personal and credit card details, or call while posing as customer service to ask for passwords and one-time passcodes.
warning_signs_en: Texts with suspicious links or urgent requests for passwords/passcodes;Callers who ask for personal financial details;Web addresses that do not match the official domain
advice_en: Never click suspicious links or share passwords and passcodes;Verify the institution through its official channels;Turn on two-factor authentication and check account activity regularly

definition_en: Scammers pose as couriers, toll payment systems (such as HKeToll), telecom operators or utilities, sending phishing texts about parcels, overdue payments or expiring reward points.
how_it_works_en: Scammers send texts claiming a parcel cannot be delivered or a fee is unpaid, with a phishing link that asks for credit card details or a small "handling fee", then take over the account or steal money.
warning_signs_en: Texts asking for a small payment or to click a link;Sender names that look official but come from suspicious numbers;Pressure to act within a short time
advice_en: Do not click links in unsolicited texts;Check parcel or payment status in the official app or website;Treat "overdue payment" notices with caution

definition_en: Scammers pose as government departments (e.g. Immigration, Department of Health), police or judicial officers, claiming the victim is involved in a case or government matter and demanding information or payment.
how_it_works_en: Scammers call or text as officials, claim the victim's identity has been misused or linked to money laundering, and demand personal data, a transfer to a "safe account", or installation of remote-control software.
warning_signs_en: Claims that you are involved in a case and must keep it secret;Requests to transfer money to a "safe account";Requests to install unknown apps or share your screen
advice_en: Government departments do not ask for transfers or passwords by phone;Hang up and call back through the official number;Never share personal data or install unknown software

definition_en: Scammers use the name of charities (such as World Vision) to collect donations or personal data, citing child sponsorship, donations or disaster relief.
how_it_works_en: Scammers pose as a charity raising funds for child sponsorship or disaster relief, persuading victims to donate or provide personal and payment details; the money goes to the scammers' accounts.
warning_signs_en: Requests for donations or payment details without verification;Payment to a personal rather than an organisational account;Urgent pressure to donate
advice_en: Donate only through official channels;Check the charity's registration and receiving account;Be cautious with unsolicited fundraising requests

definition_en: Investment fraud involving securities, forex, precious metals, virtual assets or cryptocurrency platforms, including fake trading platforms and Ponzi schemes.
how_it_works_en: Scammers promote high-return investments via social media or ads and get victims to deposit money on a fake platform; early "profits" are shown, then withdrawals are blocked or the platform disappears. Celebrity endorsements and fake apps are often used.
warning_signs_en: Promises of high returns with low risk;Requests to download unknown apps or transfer to personal accounts;Extra fees demanded before you can withdraw
advice_en: Use only licensed platforms and check their licence;Be wary of guaranteed returns;Do not trust online investment "mentors" or chat groups

definition_en: Scams on shopping, second-hand trading, ticketing or subscription platforms, such as non-delivery after payment, fake shops, payment phishing and credit card fraud.
how_it_works_en: Scammers attract buyers with cheap or scarce goods, then disappear after payment or send fake items; others pose as subscription services to steal payment details through phishing links.
warning_signs_en: Prices far below market value;Requests to pay outside the platform;Sellers who refuse to meet or give fake tracking details
advice_en: Use the platform's protected payment where possible;Check seller ratings and shop details;Do not transfer money directly to strangers

definition_en: Scams or disputes involving health supplements, weight-loss or consumer products, or multi-level marketing, such as false health claims, misdescribed goods or recruitment-based schemes.
how_it_works_en: Sellers exaggerate the effects of supplements or products and sell low-quality goods at high prices, or use multi-level marketing to collect fees by recruiting others; cases like Theranos used fake medical technology to win investment and trust.
warning_signs_en: Claims of miracle or instant results;Pressure to join as a member and recruit others;Prices far above market with no independent certification
advice_en: Be cautious of exaggerated product claims;Check the product and company background;Do not buy in bulk because of personal ties or promised returns

definition_en: Scams that use jobs, part-time work, data labelling, "order brushing" or surveys as bait to obtain fees or personal data, or to use victims' accounts for money laundering.
how_it_works_en: Scammers offer easy, well-paid work, then ask for training fees or deposits, ask to "borrow" the victim's bank account to receive money, or set fake tasks that require the victim to advance funds.
warning_signs_en: Hired without an interview and asked to pay;Asked to advance money or lend a bank account;Vague job duties with unusually high pay
advice_en: Be wary of jobs that require payment first;Never lend your bank account or receive money for others;Check the company and the recruitment channel

definition_en: Scams in which scammers build relationships through dating apps, social media or live-streaming platforms and then obtain money, including "pig butchering" schemes.
how_it_works_en: Scammers build trust on dating platforms, then ask for money for emergencies, joint investments or live-stream gifts; "pig butchering" uses romance as bait before steering victims to fake investment platforms.
warning_signs_en: Fast-moving romance followed by requests for money;Requests to transfer money for investments or emergencies;Refusal to video call or meet in person
advice_en: Be cautious when an online contact you have never met mentions money;Do not transfer money or invest at their suggestion;Check suspicious requests with family or friends

definition_en: Scammers take over WhatsApp, Telegram, WeChat, Facebook or similar accounts through phishing or verification codes, then impersonate the owner to borrow money from contacts; short-link phishing and fake tech support (e.g. Geek Squad) are also included.
how_it_works_en: Scammers obtain verification codes via phishing links or fake customer service, log in to the victim's messaging account, and then pose as the victim to ask friends for money or to buy prepaid cards.
warning_signs_en: Unexpected requests for verification codes or suspicious links;A friend's account suddenly asking to borrow money or buy prepaid cards;Unknown log-ins to your account
advice_en: Turn on two-factor authentication;Never share verification codes with anyone;Confirm with the person directly through another channel before transferring money

definition_en: Scams that use AI face-swapping, synthetic voices or deepfake videos to impersonate celebrities, relatives or organisations.
how_it_works_en: Scammers use AI to fake celebrity images or relatives' voices in video calls or ads to induce investments or transfers, or impersonate AI tool brands to spread fake apps and collect data.
warning_signs_en: Unnatural video, with lips and voice out of sync;Weak reasons for urgent transfers;Difficulty confirming the person's real identity
advice_en: Watch for anything odd in video calls;Verify identity another way before any large transfer;Download apps only from official sources

definition_en: Searches about scam compounds in Southeast Asia (e.g. Cambodia, Myanmar), the "KK Park" compound and human trafficking, including related news coverage.
how_it_works_en: Criminal groups lure people to Southeast Asia with high-paying job offers, then detain them and force them to carry out scams; related news reports drew wide public attention and searches.
warning_signs_en: Well-paid overseas jobs that need no experience;Instructions to travel via borders or unofficial crossings;Vague job details and suspicious contact methods
advice_en: Check overseas job offers and the employer's background;Do not trust high-paying overseas recruitment ads;Seek help immediately if you suspect you have been deceived

definition_en: Searches for anti-scam agencies, reporting hotlines, reporting tools and anti-scam information, such as the Anti-Deception Coordination Centre and Scameter.
how_it_works_en: The public can report suspicious calls, websites or scams through official channels and get anti-scam information and help.
advice_en: If something looks suspicious, call the Anti-Deception Coordination Centre's "Anti-Scam Helpline 18222" or check it with Scameter

definition_en: General scam-related terms, definitions, news, films, games, or terms unrelated to scams (e.g. "scampi"), which do not point to a specific scam method, platform or organisation.
Scam-related searches that do not fit the categories above, including specific cases, unidentifiable abbreviations or names, and vague references to scams.
